question.worked_solution:
First, we clear the rational expressions by multiplying both sides of the inequality by the lowest common positive multiple of the denominators:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{2y-8}{3} & \le \frac{8-2y}{4} \\ 12\cdot (\frac{2y-8}{3}) & \le 12\cdot (\frac{8-2y}{4}) \\ 4\cdot (2y-8) & \le 3\cdot (8-2y) \\ 8y-32 & \le 24-6y\end{aligned}
$$

Then, we apply the addition and multiplication principles:

$$
\begin{aligned}8y-32 & \le 24-6y \\ 8y-32+6y & \le 24-6y+6y \\ 14y-32 & \le 24 \\ 14y-32+32 & \le 24+32 \\ 14y & \le 56 \\ \frac{14y}{14} & \le \frac{56}{14} \\ y & \le 4\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the solution is $y\le 4.$
